questions.explain: Identity has 1s on the main diagonal and 0s everywhere else. The all-ones matrix is not "multiply by 1"; the anti-diagonal one swaps components.

questions.q: With $v = (3, -2, 1.5)$, what is $(I_3 v)_2$, the second component of $I_3 v$?
questions.explain: Row 2 of $I_3$ is $(0, 1, 0)$, so $(Iv)_2 = 0 \cdot 3 + 1 \cdot (-2) + 0 \cdot 1.5 = -2$: it selects exactly $v_2$. Summing all components (2.5) is the all-ones-row trap.

questions.q: For a square matrix $A$, which statement is true?
questions.explain: Identity is the neutral element of matrix multiplication, on the left and on the right — the matrix version of multiplying by 1.

questions.q: Geometrically, what does the identity transformation do to the plane?
options: Scales it by 1 in x and 0 in y
Reflects it across the line $y = x$
Nothing — no rotation, no scaling, no shear, no flip
questions.explain: Every vector comes out unchanged, so positions, lengths, angles and directions are all preserved.
